{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"eb8b3bbea2ff98a8afc6175d70b0c0ca87beefbba0b1f26b04a4f3ab4990f05e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:38","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Turning merging and passing","heading":"C — Turning merging and passing","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Turning merging and passing

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Before turning, slow enough to control the vehicle, stay in its lane and react to unexpected hazards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Watch for pedestrians and traffic on the road being entered, and follow signs or markings specifying turn lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
On a two-lane, two-way road, begin a left turn as near the centerline as possible and a right turn near the right edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
On a multilane road, start left turns from the left lane and right turns from the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
When entering a road with several lanes in the intended direction, turn into the nearest lane for that direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Complete the turn safely before changing into another lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
A center lane with solid outer and broken inner lines on both sides is for left turns only. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Drivers in either direction use the shared center lane to begin a left turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
A driver turning left from a cross street may end the turn in the shared center lane before joining through traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
When entering a center turn lane, watch for opposing center-lane traffic and vehicles entering from driveways or streets on the left. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
When turning left from a driveway into a center lane, watch through traffic from the left and center-lane vehicles preparing turns from either direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
Signal left at least three to four seconds before entering a center turn lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A01
Avoid entering a center turn lane too early because traveling in it longer increases head-on conflict risk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A01
Enter the center turn lane completely without leaving the vehicle's rear in a through lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A01
Turn from the center lane only when safe, after checking opposing lane users and a sufficiently large gap across traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A01
For a safe turn, signal three to four seconds ahead, use the proper starting lane, control speed and finish in the proper lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
A U-turn is permitted only where it does not endanger other traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
For a U-turn, approaching drivers from every direction must be at least 500 feet away and able to see you clearly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
Do not make a U-turn on a curve, near or approaching a hillcrest, or where a NO U-TURN sign prohibits it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
A right turn on red requires stopping, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, a clear path and no NO TURN ON RED restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
A left turn on red between one-way streets is allowed after stopping if traffic is clear and no NO TURN ON RED sign prohibits it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
The traffic gap needed to cross depends on road conditions, weather and approaching traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A02
Stopping partway across a street is safe only if a center-median turning lane can hold the entire vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A02
Before crossing or turning, make sure vehicles or pedestrians will not block the path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A02
Even with green, wait outside a blocked intersection until the vehicle can clear it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A02
Before pulling out ahead of a signaling vehicle, wait until its driver actually begins turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A02
Use added caution when crossing near hills or curves that restrict seeing or being seen. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A02
A highway merge requires enough open space to join the traffic stream safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A02
Acceleration lanes run beside through lanes so entering traffic can approach traffic speed and be seen before merging. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A02
Passing a vehicle ahead within an acceleration lane is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A02
To merge from an acceleration lane, signal, find a gap, reach traffic speed and enter that gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0050]

Misconceptions: signaling does not make a turn safe by itself; green does not permit entering a blocked intersection; a center turn lane can contain opposing traffic.
Mnemonics: signal, position, control speed and finish in the proper lane.
Glossary: acceleration lane builds speed before merging; a center turn lane serves left turns from both directions; a U-turn reverses travel direction.
